content: Bishop Auckland General Hospital is a relatively small yet modern NHS district general hospital. It primarily serves a rural catchment area. The hospital was inaugurated in 2002 and initially had approximately 286 beds, although the number of beds fluctuates over time. In recent years, the hospital has been at the center of significant controversy due to a perceived decline in the range of services it offers. The hospital operates under the County Durham and Darlington Foundation Trust. Neonates requiring specialized care are now transferred to Darlington Memorial Hospital. Additionally, Ward 3, which was dedicated to haematology, has been shut down. The number of surgical beds has been significantly reduced, and the hospital now primarily handles minor surgical procedures, many of which are performed as day cases. Despite these changes, the overall quality of services provided by the County Durham and Darlington Foundation Trust has been rated as good by the Healthcare Commission. The trust also includes two other major hospitals: Darlington Memorial Hospital and the University Hospital of North Durham. Bishop Auckland General Hospital continues to provide several essential services. It maintains an Accident and Emergency (A&E) department, performs elective surgeries and day surgeries, and offers a variety of acute medical specialties, including diabetes care, endocrinology, cardiology, and respiratory medicine. The hospital is equipped with a Critical Care Unit, which includes both Intensive Therapy Unit (ITU) and Coronary Care Unit (CCU) beds. It also provides general rehabilitation services for inpatients. Furthermore, the hospital houses a dedicated stroke unit, a rehabilitation daycare center, and a chemotherapy day unit.
